To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chromium levels in hair or urine of school children are inversely associated with neuropsychological development.
exposure to chromium is associated with lower IQ scores and increased latency in neuropsychological tests in school-age children.

(1) chromium exposure was associated with a significant decrease in IQ in school-aged children, (2) chromium was associated with an increase in reaction time in the RTT in boys and girls, (3) chromium was associated to an increase in the percentage of omission in the SAT in girls, and (4) chromium was associated in girls to an increase in latency in the SAT.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact of chromium on neuropsychological performance in children, and the results of our study provide new information about the effects of chromium exposure on the neuropsychological development of children.
the impact of chromium exposure on the neurodevelopment of schoolchildren.
the neurodevelopment of children exposed to high levels of chromium in their urine and hair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chromium is associated with neuropsychological development.
there is an inverse relationship between chromium levels and IQ, and that this relationship is also present in the CPT, RTT, and SAT.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results obtained from the present study indicate that the neuropsychological development of school-aged children living in areas with high levels of chromium contamination in the air, soil, and water is impaired.
children exposed to higher levels of chromium in the environment are likely to show lower scores in the WISC-4, SAT, CPT and RTT, and higher latencies in the SAT and RTT, than their peers.
the exposure of school-age children to chromium in urine and hair is associated with deficits in cognitive and executive functions, such as attention, memory, and executive function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of chromium on children are not limited to the early years of life, but also affect their neuropsychological development.
the use of chromium-based pigments in the ceramic industry should be restricted.
